column1: # *** THE FAMILIES THIS ARCHIVE HAS PAGES FOR, besides the Taylors (their own page is /taylor/). 17 October 2026. ***
# WHAT A ROW IS. One surname line in the register, and the places in this archive that already tell its story. The
# page at /families/<slug>/ is BUILT from site/src/data/people.json at build time - who carries the name, where, when,
# how the archive knows them, which other families they are joined to - so a count on a page cannot drift from the
# register. Nothing about a family is typed here except which spellings the archive treats as one name and where it
# has already written the family up.
# forms   the spellings that count as this name, '|'-separated. Only folds the archive has already made: Fernandez ->
#         Fernandes and Gonzalez -> Gonzales/Gonsales are in data/namefold.json (kit namefold.py); Brayley/Brailey are one
#         family because John BRAILEY's daughter is Mary Ann Hellen BRAYLEY in the register's own father edge. Nothing here
#         is folded by a sound-alike rule, and ZALDUANDO is NOT folded into ZALDUONDO (the archive has not decided it).
# group   line = the name is on the direct line of descent (the register's `isLine`, or an ancestor of it, or a spouse
#         of it); research = the archive's own research files and /uruguay/ follow the name, and it has at least eight
#         published people.
# read    label~href pairs, '|'-separated: the pages in THIS archive that already write the family up. Labels are the
#         section headings. Every href is checked by the build (links and anchors).
# WHO IS LISTED. Never a living person, never a person held out of publication (people.json `noindex`): the template
# drops them before it counts, so a family page makes nobody easier to find than their own page does.
